extracted.intended_audience: news consumers, researchers, and fact-checkers seeking source bias and credibility information
extracted.subtask_description: A single-source profile evaluating a news aggregator (SmartNews) on bias, factual reporting, credibility, and related metadata, with narrative analysis explaining the ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Rating — LEAST BIASED
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition given on page: "These sources have minimal bias and use very few loaded words (wording that attempts to influence an audience by appealing to emotion or stereotypes). The reporting is factual and usually sourced. These are the most credible media sources." Example application: SmartNews is rated Least biased because it curates from both right and left sources; the page notes a slight overall tilt left in total count. (Shows numeric score -0.8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual Reporting — MIXED
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation on page: SmartNews is rated Mixed for factual reporting because some of the sources it curates have Mixed factual ratings themselves; this is attributed to the individual sources rather than SmartNews. The page explicitly links factual-reporting rating to whether sources fail fact checks. (Shows numeric score 4.8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: MBFC Credibility Rating
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A summarized credibility level assigned by MBFC for the source. The page does not give a full definition here, but presents it as a distinct evaluative metric alongside bias and factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic/Popularity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists traffic/popularity as a descriptive metric (here 'High Traffic'), used as contextual metadata about the source's reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorizes the kind of media entity being evaluated (e.g., website, broadcast, print). Used as part of the profile metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country and Country Freedom Rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Country: Japan; MBFC’s Country Freedom Rating: MOSTLY FREE
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the source's country of origin and a country-level freedom rating. This contextualizes media environment factors that may affect reporting and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership / Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funded through in-app advertising and owned by SmartNews, Inc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the profile: ownership and funding model are presented as part of evaluating/understanding potential influences on the outlet (e.g., commercial funding sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: History / Mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Founded in 2012 and based in Tokyo. Mission (from about page): "to discover and deliver quality stories to the world"; algorithms evaluate articles, social signals, and human interactions to deliver top stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background and stated mission are included to contextualize editorial approach and claimed standards (impartial, trending, trustworthy). This can inform readers' assessment of intent vs. observed practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation Source-Mix as Bias Indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment method: evaluate the ideological range of sources the aggregator curates (e.g., CNN on the left and Fox News on the right, plus Left-Center, Right-Center, and Least Biased sources like Reuters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance from analysis: when an aggregator pulls from both left and right, MBFC may consider it 'least biased'; however, if a numerical count shows imbalance (slightly more from left), that is noted. Also, factual-rating of curated sources affects the aggregator's factual-reporting rating. The page emphasizes that bias/factual ratings of individual curated sources determine the bias/factual profile of content a user sees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of Updates / Transparency of Rating Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Last Updated: December 20, 2024 (and initial review dated 9/7/2017).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MBFC includes review and update dates on the profile; this is an explicit practice indicating currency and transparency of the rating process.
